security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, documented authentication checks, or report fields rather than dangerous behavior. The fallback setup clones an unpinned external repository and subsequently executes its Python module, creating a supply-chain risk. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection in SKILL.md; the external implementation was not included for review.

remediation.issue: Fallback setup clones an unpinned repository and runs its code with local permissions and potentially an API credential.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited commit, verify the checkout, and obtain user approval before downloading or executing external code.

content.user_title: Track Emerging AI Names Across Daily Signals
content.value_statement: New AI models, products, and repositories appear across scattered sources every day. This skill guides new-term-radar collection and turns observed signals into a deduplicated report.
actual_capabilities: Guides daily collection across configured X accounts, Hugging Face, GitHub breakouts, and sitemaps using new-term-radar.
Provides a faster sources command limited to X and Hugging Face.
Directs reports to rank names by multiple signals and name score, with evidence and source links.
Filters low-scoring names when judging runs and excludes leads already marked as known.
Separates breakout repositories from new names and discloses failed or skipped collection signals.
Provides a free command to inspect stored leads without starting another collection run.
limitations: Requires an external new-term-radar checkout and Python 3.10 or newer; its implementation is not included in this skill.
Without an AIsa key, X collection and name judging are unavailable.
The first run builds snapshots, so change-based coverage is limited; later reports depend on configured sources.
Does not measure search demand or verify claims beyond the collected examples.

use_cases.title: Prepare a daily AI briefing
use_cases.description: Collect emerging names with source links and signal strength for an editorial research queue.

use_cases.title: Find names for keyword research
use_cases.description: Gather newly observed model and product names before performing separate search-demand analysis.

use_cases.title: Monitor repository momentum
use_cases.description: Review newly observed GitHub breakouts and compare their evidence with other collected signals.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect saved leads
prompt_templates.prompt: Show stored leads from the last day without running new collection. Include available evidence and identify missing information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review existing results without collection costs.

prompt_templates.title: Collect a daily report
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a daily AI listening report. Confirm setup and estimated cost first, then rank observed names and disclose collection gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: run the standard daily workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Check faster sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use sources mode for X and Hugging Face only. Report new names with links and explain any unavailable sources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: request a narrower collection run.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize research candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Using existing listening results, prioritize names seen by multiple signals. Exclude known leads and provide evidence for separate keyword research.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare an evidence-based research shortlist without another collection run.

output_examples.input: What should I expect from the first daily run?
output_examples.output: The first run builds comparison snapshots. Expect GitHub breakout coverage and limited change-based results, not a complete daily trend picture.

output_examples.input: Prepare a report without an AIsa key.
output: Available sources: Hugging Face, GitHub, and configured sitemaps.
Unavailable signals: X posts and name judging.
Report observed names with available evidence and clearly disclose these coverage gaps.

best_practices: Review and pin the external radar checkout before execution; confirm the account list and estimated API cost.
Keep snapshots between runs and disclose first-run limitations or skipped signals.
Use collected examples and links for descriptions; validate search demand in a separate research step.
anti_patterns: Running collection twice consecutively and treating the second delta as a full daily report.
Interpreting limited first-run results or missing authentication as evidence of low AI activity.
Adding names from memory or presenting signal strength as measured search demand.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The instructions require Python 3.10 or newer and a new-term-radar checkout. They state that no additional Python packages are required.

faq.question: Is an AIsa key required?
faq.answer: A key enables X collection and name judging. Without one, only Hugging Face, GitHub, and sitemap signals run.

faq.question: How much does a daily run cost?
faq.answer: The skill estimates about 0.003 USD and 10 seconds per X account. Its 35-account example estimates 0.11 USD and six minutes.

faq.question: Why is the first report limited?
faq.answer: The first run creates snapshots for later comparisons. It reports GitHub breakouts and limited additional results.

faq.question: Does this measure keyword search demand?
faq.answer: No. It collects observed names and source signals. Search-demand analysis requires a separate research step.

faq.question: Does the skill include the collection implementation?
faq.answer: No. It directs execution of an external repository. The fallback clone is unpinned, so review and pin that code before execution.
